audit_findings.title: Post-Copra valuation uses a pre-closing capital structure
audit_findings.magnitude: $140 million cash, $35 million Common Stock, and $45 million-$100 million earnout payable in 2029
audit_findings.mechanism: The cash consideration reduces the equity bridge, stock consideration increases shares, and the earnout creates future cash and share claims; Copra's operating economics are absent from OE and growth.
audit_findings.evidence: We may issue additional capital stock in connection with financings, acquisitions, investments, our equity incentive plans, or otherwise, which will dilute other stockholders.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter mismatch, not merely a possibility. The valuation is dated after closing but uses June 30 cash and a July 21 share count. The filed acquisition disclosure quantifies material consideration, including cash equal to 19.8% of the $707 million base equity value. Those financing effects lower value per share, while excluding Copra's acquired earnings and assets may understate value, so the combined direction is mixed. A post-closing valuation could change the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Rerun with the closing share issuance, $140 million cash payment, purchase-price adjustments, fair-valued earnout, assumed assets and liabilities, transaction costs, and a post-closing balance sheet; separately incorporate supportable Copra OE.

audit_findings.title: The full cash and short-term-investment balance may not be distributable surplus
audit_findings.magnitude: $278.64 million added to the bridge; $140 million subsequently paid for Copra, equal to 19.8% of the $707 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Non-surplus cash is incorrectly added dollar-for-dollar in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: We generally operate with a small target cash balance, and when that level is exceeded, we invest any excess in interest generating investments with generally short maturities consistent with our projected cash business needs.
audit_findings.explanation: The $140 million acquisition payment demonstrates that at least a material portion of the June 30 cash balance was committed rather than distributable surplus. The entire $278.64 million addition represents 39.4% of base equity value. Minimum operating cash and other committed uses remain unquantified, so the total overstatement cannot yet be established.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile June 30 cash through closing, remove the $140 million payment and other committed uses, identify unrestricted post-closing cash, and retain only cash exceeding a documented operating-liquidity requirement.

audit_findings.title: The stated diluted-share ceiling is not an actual ceiling
audit_findings.magnitude: 302,949 non-vested PSUs at June 30, 2026, or 0.49% of the 61.70459 million-share denominator; excess payout shares unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Above-target PSU vesting would increase the fully diluted share denominator and reduce value per share.
audit_findings.evidence: Certain performance share unit awards allow for the issuance of shares in excess of the target award amount when performance results exceed specified thresholds.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that PSU awards can issue more than their target amounts, so describing a target-based denominator as a ceiling is erroneous. It does not disclose the maximum multipliers or incremental shares, however, so the record cannot establish whether the omitted dilution is material.
audit_findings.action: Obtain award-level maximum payout multipliers, calculate maximum incremental PSU shares, add post-period grants and acquisition-related awards, and rerun per-share values using the reconciled ceiling.

audit_findings.title: Explicit 2025 one-offs may depress the mandatory anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $3.6 million net pre-tax expense; a conservative dollar-for-dollar OE sensitivity raises base value from $11.46 to about $12.28 per share and bull value from $12.71 to about $13.67
audit_findings.mechanism: Removing net nonrecurring expense would increase anchor OE and proportionally increase operating PV in every scenario.
audit_findings.evidence: For the year ended December 31, 2025, the amount reflects $2.4 million related to a one-time 2023 incentive program that is measured based on full-year 2025 performance relative to 2022 structured differently from our other ongoing employee incentive programs, $1.2 million of overlapping rent expense related to our New York City office, $0.2 million of impairment loss related to Runa, and a gain of $0.2 million from a sale of intellectual property.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing identifies $3.8 million of one-time or transitional costs and a $0.2 million nonrecurring gain, for a net $3.6 million pre-tax expense. It is unresolved whether every item remains in the $30.5 million OE anchor. Even treating the entire pre-tax amount as additional OE—an intentionally generous upper bound—leaves the highest scenario near $13.67 per share, far below the $55.13 market price, so it cannot change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Trace all four items through the OE calculation and rerun a symmetric sensitivity removing both the nonrecurring costs and gain; retain the filed anchor as the primary case unless the methodology permits normalization.

audit_findings.title: Legacy service and exit warrants require a final denominator reconciliation
audit_findings.magnitude: 8.113105 million shares labeled Common Stock with Exit Warrants, equal to 13.1% of the 61.70459 million-share denominator; any separate surviving claim is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A separate warrant, settlement, preference, or exit-payment claim would require additional shares or an equity-bridge deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: Basic net income per share is computed by dividing net income by the weighted average number of common shares and service warrants outstanding during each period.
audit_findings.explanation: The 8.113105 million shares are already included in issued common stock and therefore are not demonstrated omitted dilution. The EPS policy separately refers to service warrants, but the supplied record does not establish whether any warrant right survives independently of the counted shares. Because the labeled class is large, an additional economic claim could be material, but its existence and amount remain unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile issued and outstanding shares to the transfer-agent register and inspect the service- and exit-warrant instruments for separate exercise shares, cash settlement, preferences, or exit-payment rights.

audit_findings.title: Public-benefit obligations can divert future economics from common equity
audit_findings.mechanism: Incremental stakeholder spending or financially suboptimal capital allocation could reduce future OE, growth economics, reinvestment returns, and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Therefore, we may take actions that we believe will be in the best interests of those stakeholders materially affected by our specific benefit purpose, even if those actions do not maximize our financial results.
audit_findings.explanation: The legal balancing obligation is demonstrated, but no incremental commitment or omitted current-period expense is identified.
